title: Memory vs Storage
about: Tell the desk from the cupboard, and spot when each one is full.

cards.sentence: **RAM** is like a desk: fast, but wiped clean when the power goes off.
**Storage** is like a cupboard: it keeps your apps, photos and saved files, even with the power off.

cards.explanation: Saved and installed things live in **storage**, which keeps them with the power off. Anything that was only open lived in **RAM**, which is wiped when the power goes. (That's why many apps save your work for you every few minutes.)
cards.hint: For each one, ask: was it saved or installed, or was it only open on the screen?
cards.nudge: Saving is what keeps things safe. Anything that was only open, and never saved, doesn't survive the power going off.

cards.sentence: Both are measured in **gigabytes (GB)**, and storage usually has many times more than RAM.

cards.prompt: Run the **racing game** and the **music** on this 4 GB phone, with no lag.
cards.explanation: Every open app needs room in **RAM**, and the phone's own system needs some too. With the game on, everything needed 5 GB, more than the phone's 4 GB, so it lagged. Closing the video call made room. (A laptop with full RAM slows down instead, as it shuffles things out to storage.)
cards.hint: Every open app takes room in RAM. The game and the music must stay on, so which app don't you need?
cards.nudge: Still lagging? The open apps need more than 4 GB. Keep the game and music on, and close the other one.

cards.prompt: Every app you open takes up some room in RAM.
cards.explanation: **True.** Each open app needs space on the desk. Open too many, and RAM fills up and the device lags.
cards.hint: Think about what happened to the RAM bar when you turned the game on.
cards.nudge: Look back at the phone: what happened to the RAM bar each time an app went on?

cards.title: A real RAM stick

photo.alt: A green laptop RAM stick with a label in the middle, black memory chips and a row of gold contacts along its bottom edge.

cards.caption: A laptop RAM stick (8 GB). Phones and many thin laptops solder their RAM on instead.

cards.prompt: You're about to photograph a rainbow, and a message pops up.

steps.text: **"Not enough space. Can't save photo."** Which kind of space has run out?

choices.consequence: Right. Saving a photo needs room in storage, and yours is full.
RAM only holds what's open right now. A photo you *save* goes to storage, and that's what's full.

steps.text: The rainbow won't last long. How do you make room quickly?

choices.consequence: That frees **RAM**, not storage. The message comes straight back.

choices.text: Delete big videos you've backed up (copied somewhere else)
choices.consequence: Videos take up lots of storage, so deleting a few you've backed up frees plenty of room. You get the shot!
Restarting wipes RAM, but every file in storage is still there. It's still full.

cards.explanation: A "not enough space" message when you **save** something means **storage** is full. Only removing files frees storage. Closing apps and restarting only clear RAM.
cards.hint: The message appeared when you tried to save a photo. Which kind of space keeps saved files?

cards.prompt: A film you download needs free space in ___.

options.nudge: RAM only holds what's open right now, and it's wiped at power off. A download is kept for later.
The CPU follows instructions; it doesn't keep files. Where do saved things live?

cards.explanation: Downloads are saved in **storage**, so they need free storage space. How much RAM you have makes no difference.
cards.hint: A download has to still be there tomorrow. Where do saved files live?
cards.nudge: A download has to survive switching off. Which kind of space keeps things?

cards.prompt: A laptop on for weeks feels slow. Why does a restart help?

options.nudge: Restarting doesn't touch storage: every file is still there afterwards. Which space is wiped when the power goes off?
A restart doesn't change the CPU at all. Think about the desk: what happens to it when the power goes off?

cards.explanation: Turning off wipes **RAM**, including leftovers from apps that didn't tidy up after themselves. Your files in **storage** stay exactly where they were, and the CPU's speed doesn't change.
cards.hint: Which kind of space is wiped when the power goes off?

cards.prompt: Your phone has **40 GB of free storage**, but something's wrong.

steps.text: Your game keeps **reloading from scratch**, and the music keeps stopping. What's running short?

choices.consequence: Yes. When RAM fills up, the phone closes apps in the background to make room, so they have to reload.
There's 40 GB free, so storage isn't the problem. Apps reloading is a sign the **desk** is full.

steps.text: What's the best fix for right now?

choices.text: Close the apps you aren't using
choices.consequence: That frees RAM for the game and the music. They stop reloading.
Photos live in storage, which had plenty of room. RAM is still just as full.
That's one more app filling RAM, and "booster" apps are often junk or worse.

cards.explanation: Apps that keep **reloading** are a sign of full **RAM**, not full storage. Closing apps you aren't using gives the others room. Deleting files only frees storage.
cards.hint: Notice there's 40 GB of storage free. Think back to what happened when the phone's RAM got too full.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- **RAM** is the fast desk for what's open. Power off wipes it.
- **Storage** keeps apps and files until you delete them.
- Full RAM? Close apps. Full storage? Delete files you've [[backed up|backup]].

Next: the [[CPU]], the part that does the work.
